body:
## Summary

During post-install/re-entry testing, `sudo noemaforge safe-start --wait --llm-profile=runtime_only` started the safe core services successfully, but also left gateway/toolproxy systemd units enabled. This is surprising when the machine is explicitly in manual boot mode.

This is an install/startup policy issue: a one-shot safe-start used for validation should not silently change persistent autostart state unless the operator requested persistence.

## Environment

- NoemaForge CLI: `0.33.0`
- Branch: `release/0.33.0-dev`
- Boot mode before re-entry: manual
- Command used: `sudo noemaforge safe-start --wait --llm-profile=runtime_only`

## Evidence

Before re-entry, no NF units were active and unit files were disabled:

```text
UNIT FILE                               STATE    PRESET
noemaforge-autostart-wogui.service      disabled enabled
noemaforge-llama@.service               disabled enabled
noemaforge-llm-gateway.service          disabled enabled
noemaforge-memsentinel.service          disabled enabled
noemaforge-toolproxy.service            disabled enabled
noemaforge-autostart-gui.timer          disabled enabled
noemaforge-llm-backends-manager.timer   disabled enabled
noemaforge-modelscan.timer              disabled enabled
```

`boot-mode show` reported manual mode:

```text
NoemaForge boot mode: manual

Systemd autostart:
  gui timer:    disabled
  gui service:  static
  wogui:        disabled

Autostart profiles:
  gui:   runtime_only
  wogui: bootstrap_cpu_llm
```

After `safe-start runtime_only`, service status showed enabled units:

```text
noemaforge-llm-gateway.service - loaded; enabled; active running
noemaforge-toolproxy.service   - loaded; enabled; active running
```

The safe-start log also says:

```text
[noemaforge-safe-start] enabling safe core services...
[noemaforge-safe-start] starting gateway/toolproxy...
```

## Expected behavior

For a one-shot post-install validation command:

```text
safe-start --llm-profile=runtime_only
```

should start the services for the current session, but should not persistently enable them unless the operator also requests an explicit enable/autostart action.

Expected distinction:

```text
noemaforge safe-start ...             # start now, no persistence change
noemaforge manager enable             # persistently enable manager/modelscan policy
noemaforge dashboard autostart-enable # persistently enable dashboard autostart
noemaforge boot-mode set ...          # change boot/autostart policy
```

## Suggested fix

1. Split `start now` from `enable on boot` in `safe-start`.
2. Add `--enable` or `--persist` if persistent enablement is desired.
3. In manual boot mode, default to non-persistent start.
4. Update docs/help text so post-install validation does not accidentally alter boot persistence.
5. Add a regression test: manual boot mode + `safe-start runtime_only` must not change unit-file enabled/disabled state.

## Why this matters

Manual boot mode is used during recovery and controlled NF re-entry. If `safe-start` mutates persistent systemd state, a diagnostic action can unexpectedly change what starts after reboot, making UAT and recovery harder to reason about.
title: safe-start runtime_only mutates persistent systemd enablement despite manual boot mode
